title: 11 Checkout Essentials
intro: Most cart abandonment comes from surprises and friction, not indecision. Baymard's survey of US shoppers puts unexpected costs at the top by a wide margin.

learn.title: Why shoppers abandon
learn.text:
From Baymard's survey as cited in 2024:

• Extra costs too high — **47%**
• Forced account creation — **25%**
• Delivery too slow — **24%**
• Didn't trust the site — **19%**
• Checkout too long — **18%**
• Couldn't see the total up front — **17%**
• Returns policy — **16%**
• Site errors or crashes — **14%**

Baymard updates these figures regularly — check the current release before quoting them.

try.q: What is the single biggest reason shoppers abandon checkout?
options: Being forced to create an account
A checkout flow with too many steps
try.explain: 47% in the cited survey — nearly twice the next reason.

learn.title: Price, account, delivery
learn.text:
**Show all costs up front** and every change as it happens; keep a running total visible.

**Make guest checkout prominent** and offer an account after the purchase, not before.

**State delivery times before checkout**, not on the final screen.

try.q: When should you offer account creation?
try.explain: Forced account creation is the second-largest abandonment reason.

left.label: Surprises that lose the sale
items: Shipping added at the last step

learn.title: Trust, length and recovery
learn.text:
Earn trust at the payment step with recognisable security cues and clear assurances about data.

Cut checkout to essentials and autofill everything you can. Offer the wallets people already use — Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal.

Make the return policy easy to find and fair. And handle errors without wiping what the user typed.

try.q: A card is declined. What should the form do?
options: Return the user to the cart
Clear the card fields for security
Offer a different payment method only
try.explain: Site errors are an abandonment cause in their own right; preserving input is basic recovery.

test.q: Where do these percentages come from?
options: A Baymard survey of US shoppers
A Nielsen Norman Group benchmark study
test.explain: And the article notes they should be re-checked before quoting. As cited in 2024.

test.q: What is the main cause of abandonment, in one word?
test.explain: Unexpected costs, hidden totals and late delivery news.

test.q: What should stay visible throughout checkout?
test.explain: Including every change as it happens.

options: Users already trust and can use them
They remove the need for a privacy policy
They are required in most European markets
test.explain: Recognition reduces both friction and distrust at the payment step.

test.q: Which two reasons sit at 19% and 18% in the cited data?
options: Didn't trust the site; checkout too long
test.explain: Trust and length sit in the middle of the list.
